m1-spec-shape-faults.title: [[gate.dispatch]] spec shape + three new spec-shape faults
m1-spec-shape-faults.imperative: In scripts/generate_spine.py: add `dispatch` support to spec_shape_faults (a new _dispatch_faults helper called per gate) refusing, before any probe: spec-dispatch-missing-field (a declared dispatch entry missing role or model, naming gate+field), spec-dispatch-unresolved-parent (a dispatch declared while the spec's top-level parent is absent/falsy -- refuse rather than emit "unknown"), spec-dispatch-undeclared (a gate with no [[gate.dispatch]] whose imperative contains run_crew.py, constellation-implementer, or constellation-reviewer). Also reserve the c-dispatch-<n> condition-id family the same way RESERVED_CONDITION_ID/c-escalation already is, so an author cannot collide with the injected ids added in m2. Add tests/test_generate_spine.py::TestDeclaredDispatchSpecShapeFaults with a VIOLATING case for each of the three faults (missing role; missing model; unresolved parent; undeclared-with-marker) and INNOCENT cases (role+model+parent all present compiles clean; no dispatch and no marker in imperative is clean) -- house style tests/test_mcp_adoption.py::_cli_only_verb_violations. Do not yet touch _compile_gate/compile_spec's emission (m2). TDD: write the failing tests first (red), observe them fail for the right reason (AttributeError/fault absent), then implement until green.

m2-emission-and-oracle.title: directives.dispatch rendering + injected command postcondition + scripts/verify_declared_dispatch.py
m2-emission-and-oracle.imperative: In _compile_gate, for each declared [[gate.dispatch]] entry render {role, model, parent} (parent from the spec's top-level parent, the same value hand_back_to already carries) into directives.dispatch, and inject one command-kind postcondition per entry (id c-dispatch-<idx>) whose command -- anchored cd <repo-root> && ..., every token shlex.quote'd -- shells out to a new scripts/verify_declared_dispatch.py. Write scripts/verify_declared_dispatch.py: it imports registry_path/load_registry/is_abandoned from scripts/run_crew.py (no second JSON parse of crew-runs.json), takes --root/--work-id/--gate/--role/--parent/--model, and refuses (nonzero exit, message naming the offending/missing entry) unless a non-abandoned crew-runs.json entry for that gate+role carries the declared parent and model. Write tests/test_declared_dispatch.py exercising the script directly against fixture registries: VIOLATING wrong-parent (realistic Admiral-looking session id), VIOLATING wrong-model, VIOLATING no-matching-entry, INNOCENT matching entry, ACCEPTED_FALSE_ALARM populated -- an abandoned entry with the wrong parent must NOT block. Also add tests/test_generate_spine.py::TestDeclaredDispatchEmission asserting directives.dispatch shape and that the injected postcondition is command-kind (never artifact), plus a driven proof (checklist_engine.start/advance) that a wrong-parent registry fixture fails advance and a matching one succeeds. TDD: red first (script/tests fail or do not exist), then implement to green.
